question: What is vendor-managed inventory?
html:
What vendor-managed inventory means

Vendor-managed inventory (VMI) means we manage a customer's lab supplies on their site. We track usage, set reorder points and restock before they run out, so the lab doesn't have to place routine orders. Our growth plan names VMI as one of the levers that moves us from a commodity distributor toward a lab supply-chain company (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

How it works in practice

  • We hold the replenishment job. We monitor stock of consumables at the customer's lab, pathology or hospital site and refill it.
  • Ordering becomes routine. Restocking follows agreed levels, not ad hoc purchase orders.
  • It pairs with digital ordering. The growth plan groups VMI with punchout ordering and private label as one supply-chain offer (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

Why it sits in the plan

LeverRole in the plan
VMIMakes accounts sticky
Private labelHigher-margin mix (19% of VWR's sales)
AI pricing toolsAbout 120 basis points added at large distributors

All three come from the growth plan's margin-from-mix argument (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

  • Target pool: 27,503 scored sites, with 713 rated Pursue and 2,317 Nurture. These are the natural VMI candidates (Thomas Scientific growth plan).
  • Margin path: The plan assumes EBITDA margin of about 11.5% by month 24 and about 12% by month 36, partly from mix. These are est., not forecasts (Thomas Scientific growth plan).

What we don't know yet

The context has no figures on our current VMI accounts, their revenue, retention or margin. These would answer that:

  • Number of sites on VMI today and their share of revenue.
  • Renewal and churn rates for VMI accounts compared with non-VMI accounts.
  • Cost to serve per VMI site, including labor and inventory carried on our books.

That last point matters. Revenue and EBITDA are already low-confidence estimates (Thomas Scientific public filings). Cash tied up in customer-site stock has to be weighed against liquidity.

With the first-lien loan maturing on Dec 14, 2027 and est. leverage of 7-10x, sticky, recurring accounts are part of the evidence lenders need to see before they refinance (Thomas Scientific public filings).

Next actions

  1. Pull a baseline of current VMI sites, revenue and retention from internal order data.
  2. Model the working-capital cost per VMI site before expanding. Sequence any expansion behind the refinancing.
  3. Flag VMI fit within the 713 Pursue sites as inside-sales books are built.
  4. Bundle VMI with punchout ordering in one offer for named-coverage accounts.
